extracted.intended_audience: Department of Defense managers, federal agency officials, congressional staff, and policy analysts concerned with federal competitive sourcing and outsourcing
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating whether recurring commercial activities should be performed by the private sector or federal government employees under OMB Circular A-76 and implementing FAIR Act requirements, including use of managed competitions (competitive sourcing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of performance source for recurring commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether recurring commercial activities should be transferred to performance by the private sector, or performance by federal government employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular defines federal policy for making this determination. Decisions focus on recurring commercial activities and whether performance should shift to private-sector contractors or remain with federal employees. (Page summary notes this as the core purpose of Circular A-76.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of inherently governmental versus non-inherently governmental activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must identify activities both inherently governmental and those not inherently governmental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAIR Act creates statutory reporting requirements requiring federal executive agencies to distinguish inherently governmental functions (which generally should not be outsourced) from activities that are not inherently governmental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of managed competitions to select service provider
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct managed competitions to determine who is best to perform the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive sourcing, implemented through managed competitions, is the mechanism by which agencies compare public-sector and private-sector proposals to decide who should perform an activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with FAIR Act reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory reporting obligations under the Federal Activities Inventory Reform Act of 1998 obligate agencies to identify and report inventories of activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must create inventories that categorize activities (inherently governmental vs not inherently governmental) and submit reports as required by the FAIR Act to provide transparency and enable managed competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Presidential Management Agenda / competitive sourcing initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive sourcing is a major initiative identified by the Presidential Management Agenda to improve management and performance of the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy decisions and implementation should be evaluated for consistency with broader management reform goals (e.g., improving efficiency and performance). The summary indicates competitive sourcing was likely to continue as a government-wide initiative.
